title: 1 · Sounds and spelling
blurb: Read Tagalog aloud from its spelling and from the pronunciation line: the vowels, ng and mga, stress and the catch.

title: 2 · Greetings and respect: po and opo
blurb: Greet anyone at any time of day, say thank you and goodbye, and show respect with po, opo and kayo.

title: 3 · ang pronouns: ako, ikaw / ka, siya, kami, tayo, kayo, sila
blurb: Say I, you, he, she, we and they in Tagalog, choose the right we, and put si before a name.

title: 4 · Introducing yourself: Ako si…, Taga-… ako
blurb: Introduce yourself: your name, where you are from, your age, and that you are learning Tagalog.

title: 5 · ito, iyan, iyon: this and that
blurb: Point at things near you, near the listener or far away, and ask what they are and how much they cost.

title: 6 · Markers: ang / si, ng / ni, sa / kay
blurb: Use the markers ang, ng and sa, and si, ni and kay for names, to show what each noun does in a sentence.

title: 7 · The linker na / -ng and ma- describing words
blurb: Describe people and things: join a describing word to its noun with the linker na or -ng, in either order.

title: 8 · ng pronouns and possession: ko, mo, niya
blurb: Say my, your, his and her, and use ko and mo after gusto and alam: Gusto ko, Hindi ko alam.

title: 9 · Questions: ba, sino, ano, saan, kailan
blurb: Ask yes-or-no questions with ba, and ask who, what, where, when, why, how, which and how much.

title: 10 · Yes and no: oo / opo, hindi, wala, huwag
blurb: Say yes and no politely, and pick the right "no" for the job: hindi, wala or huwag.

title: 11 · Numbers: native and Spanish
blurb: Count things with native Tagalog numbers, link them to nouns, and understand prices said with Spanish numbers.

title: 12 · may, mayroon, wala: there is, have
blurb: Say what there is and what you have, and say there's none, with may, mayroon and wala.

title: 13 · Family and jobs
blurb: Talk about your family, use kuya, ate, tito and tita the Filipino way, and say what people do for work.

title: 14 · sa pronouns and place: sa akin, dito, nasaan
blurb: Say "for me" and "to you", say where people and things are, and ask where something is.

title: 15 · Word order: predicate first, ay, and the little words
blurb: Build sentences in everyday Tagalog order: the new information first, then the little words in their fixed places.

title: 16 · -um- verbs (actor focus): kumain, uminom, pumunta
blurb: Say what someone did with -um- verbs: who did it, what they did it to, and where they went.

title: 17 · mag- verbs (actor focus): magluto, maglaro, magtrabaho
blurb: Say what someone did with mag- verbs, spell the hyphen in nag-aral, and keep the doer in the ang form.

title: 18 · Aspect: completed, ongoing, future
blurb: Say what you did, what you are doing and what you will do with -um- and mag- verbs.

title: 19 · gusto, ayaw, kailangan, puwede
blurb: Say what you want, don't want, need, may do and know how to do, with the right pronoun and the linker.

title: 20 · -in verbs (object focus): Kinain ko ang mangga
blurb: Say what someone did to a particular thing, with the thing as the topic: Kinain ko ang mangga.

title: 21 · Ordering food and prices
blurb: Eat with Filipinos, order at a carinderia, buy at a sari-sari store, and ask for the price.

title: 22 · Time and days: alas-tres, Lunes, kahapon, bukas
blurb: Tell the time, say how long something takes, and talk about days, yesterday, later and tomorrow.

title: 23 · Directions and transport: kaliwa, kanan, Para po!
blurb: Ask the way, follow left and right, and ride a jeepney, tricycle, taxi or Grab.

title: 24 · Requests and commands: paki-, huwag
blurb: Ask politely with paki- and Puwede po bang…, give simple commands, and say "don't" with huwag.

title: 25 · Little words: na, pa, rin / din, lang, naman
blurb: Use the little words for already, still, also, just and "how about", in the right place after the first word.

title: 26 · Comparing: mas … kaysa, pinaka-
blurb: Say that something is more, most or as … as something else: mas mura, pinakamura, kaysa.

title: 27 · Everyday Manila Tagalog and Taglish
blurb: Understand the English words and casual forms you hear every day in Manila, and know when to use them.
